notes: Arrival in Normandy 27 June per Wikipedia list (landing beach not given). Disbanded Aug 1944 for infantry replacements.

current_activity: Charnwood: two brigades pass through to take Epron and St. Contest; St. Contest and most of la Bijude are taken
notes: Event date: 8 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 314, 315). Event definition: After the opening phase of the attack on Caen, two brigades of the division pass fresh troops through to capture their second objective, the villages of Epron and St. Contest (p. 314); by the end of the day the division has taken St. Contest and what was left of la Bijude, but its other objectives still hold out (p. 315). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 314: "The two 59th Division brigades were to pass fresh troops through to capture their second objective (the villages of Epron and St. Contest)"; p. 315: "succeeded in taking St. Contest and what was left of la Bijude". Location: Epron, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Epron, the more northerly of the two villages named as the objective; St. Contest lies close by. Location support: Ellis names Epron and St. Contest as the second objective (p. 314).

current_activity: Wades the Orne near Brieux in the evening; three battalions are across before daylight and a bridge is ready by 07:30
notes: Event date: 6 August 1944, evening (Ellis, vol. I, p. 408). Event definition: In the early evening of 6 August the leading infantry of the division, with the 34th Tank Brigade and 56th Infantry Brigade under command, begin wading the Orne near Brieux; three battalions are across before daylight, the engineers bridge the river by 07:30 and a squadron of tanks fords it (p. 408). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 408: "In the early evening of August the 6th the leading infantry of the 59th Division began wading the river near Brieux and before day- light next morning three battalions were across". Location: Brieux, Orne (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names the crossing place near Brieux (p. 408).
